coach.name: Dustin Ford
coach.notes: First-year head coach; promoted from associate head coach on March 30, 2026 after John Groce left for College of Charleston. 23rd head coach in Akron MBB history. Associate head coach at Akron 2017-2026 under Groce; previously assistant at Illinois (with Groce), Ohio and Western Carolina; Ohio point guard 1998-2001; born June 11, 1978, Cambridge, Ohio. Introductory press conference April 15, 2026 at House Three Thirty with AD Dr. Andrew T. Goodrich and President R.J. Nemer. Earned first career head-coaching win Nov 2, 2026, 75-61 at Louisiana. Contract terms not found in sources read.

previews.title: Akron Picked Third in MAC Poll; Mahaffey, Staveskie Honored
previews.author: BVM Sportsdesk
previews.projected_finish: 3rd in MAC preseason poll (110 points; Miami 130, Toledo 117)
previews.summary: Akron was picked third in the MAC preseason coaches poll behind Miami and Toledo. Seniors Evan Mahaffey and Tahj Staveskie were named preseason All-MAC Second Team. Akron enters 2026-27 after three straight MAC Tournament titles and NCAA Tournament trips (2024, 2025, 2026) and is chasing a fourth straight. The piece frames the poll as a forecast, not a verdict, and says Akron must prove it can stay ahead of Miami and Toledo. Summary is AI-assisted from the GoZips release.

previews.summary: Akron opens the Dustin Ford era ranked No. 7 in the CollegeInsider.com Mid-Major Top 25 with 542 points, after being picked third in the MAC. The program has won three consecutive MAC Tournament titles and reached the NCAA Tournament in 2024, 2025 and 2026. Season opener Nov 2 at Louisiana in the MAC-SBC Challenge; home opener Nov 9 vs. Muskingum at James A. Rhodes Arena.

previews.title: Akron Opens 2026-27 Season vs. Youngstown State in Exhibition
previews.author: BVM Sportsdesk
previews.summary: Previews the Oct 27, 2026 (7 p.m. ET) home exhibition against Youngstown State, described as a first look at how new coach Dustin Ford's 'retooled' squad is taking shape. Akron leads the regular-season series 59-32 and has won 8 of the last 9 meetings; YSU won last year's exhibition 84-78 after trailing by nine at halftime. Regular season opens Nov 2 at Louisiana; home opener Nov 9 vs. Muskingum will also celebrate last season's championship. No players named. Companion GoZips release: https://gozips.com/news/2026/10/26/mens-basketball-zips-open-2026-27-campaign-with-exhibition-matchup-against-youngstown-state (not read).

previews.title: 2026-27 Mid-American Men's Basketball Overview
previews.author: Kaily "KG" Godek (Akron section)
previews.summary: Akron went 29-6 (17-1 MAC) in 2025-26 and now has a 'new looking' roster under first-year coach Dustin Ford, promoted from associate head coach after Groce left for Charleston. The piece says Ford is building the culture he wants after heavy turnover. Key pieces are returning grad forward Evan Mahaffey and three transfers: Ty Pence (Illinois State), Tahj Staveskie (Incarnate Word) and Max Burton (Western Michigan), with Burton called a key veteran resource. Departures: Tavari Johnson (Charleston), Eric Mahaffey (Cincinnati), Sharron Young (Western Kentucky); graduated Amani Lyles, Shammah Scott and Bowen Hardman. Non-conference highlight: ESPN Events Invitational in Orlando Nov 23-25 vs. Wright State, Belmont and Appalachian State.

storylines.headline: Dustin Ford era begins after Groce's exit to Charleston
storylines.detail: Groce left March 30, 2026 for College of Charleston; longtime associate head coach Ford was promoted the same day and introduced April 15. He won his first game as a head coach 75-61 at Louisiana on Nov 2, 2026.

storylines.headline: Chasing a fourth straight MAC Tournament title
storylines.detail: Akron has won three consecutive MAC Tournament championships and made the NCAA Tournament in 2024, 2025 and 2026; 2025-26 record was 29-6 (17-1 MAC). Picked 3rd in the MAC and No. 7 in the CollegeInsider Mid-Major Top 25.

storylines.headline: Heavy roster turnover: Tavari Johnson followed Groce, Eric Mahaffey to Cincinnati
storylines.detail: Johnson (Charleston), Eric Mahaffey (Cincinnati) and Sharron Young (WKU) transferred out; Lyles, Scott and Hardman graduated. Transfers Staveskie, Pence and Burton join returning Evan Mahaffey.
